label: Towards a Unified Modeling and Simulation Framework for Space Systems: Integrating Model-Based Systems Engineering with Open Source Multi-Domain Simulation Environments

evidence_quotes: Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (DIMEAS), Politecnico di Torino
source_field_summaries.label: development context
rationales: The authors are university-based; the framework is positioned for academic/resource-constrained small-satellite missions, short schedules, quick low-cost design/verification iterations, and agile/incremental development cycles.

evidence_quotes: While originally conceived as a tool to support early design phases, simulation continues to play a critical role throughout system development
source_field_summaries.label: lifecycle stage addressed
rationales: The framework and case focus on early/preliminary design and progressive logical/physical architecture; operations are addressed through ConOps and operating-mode modeling, not through deployed mission operations.

evidence_quotes: This paper presents the first version of the unified Modeling and Simulation (M&S) framework MOSAiC
source_field_summaries.label: model maturity
rationales: MOSAiC is presented as a first-version framework and demonstrated with executable simulations on a representative mission; no operational/flight validation is reported.

evidence_quotes: This work supports the broader vision of digital engineering for space systems, suggesting that a modular, standards-based approach to unifying MBSE and simulation can significantly improve system understanding and development efficiency.
source_field_summaries.label: approach classification
rationales: The approach connects architecture modeling, simulations, analyses, requirements verification, and lifecycle feedback in an open toolchain, matching integrated MBSE/digital engineering.

evidence_quotes: This paper presented a Modeling and Simulation framework for the design, analysis, and simulation of space missions and systems, with a particular focus on the application to small-satellite missions.
source_field_summaries.label: RQ1 relevance
rationales: The paper provides a general small-satellite/space-system modeling framework with EPS example, but it is not narrowly about nanosatellite/EPS reference modeling with minimal behavioral knowledge.

evidence_quotes: with the goal of improving traceability, reusability, and fidelity in the system lifecycle
source_field_summaries.label: RQ2 relevance
rationales: The paper claims traceability, reusability/reproducibility, consistency, early validation, integration-cost reduction, and technical robustness, including EPS power simulations, but outcome evidence is mostly single-case and not EPS-outcome-specific.

evidence_quotes: At this stage, the model has adequate fidelity, down to the Component level, to establish whether the system satisfies its quantitative requirements.
source_field_summaries.label: RQ3 relevance
rationales: The framework integrates pre-physical simulation-based verification and requirements linkage, including EPS power verification, but it does not model detailed EPS verification procedures, test cases, or verification matrices.

evidence_quotes: This module—and more broadly the framework—is structured around four hierarchical modeling levels, in line with the ARCADIA method: (i) Actors; (ii) System; (iii) Subsystem; (iv) Components.
source_field_summaries.label: modeling scope
rationales: The model covers stakeholder/mission needs, system/subsystem/component architecture, modes/behavior, interfaces, budgets, requirements verification, operations/ConOps, simulation, and additional orbital/link analysis domains.

evidence_quotes: functional exchanges and component exchanges have been defined, deriving the internal and external interfaces
source_field_summaries.label: model artifacts used
rationales: Reported artifacts include Capella architecture/function/exchange diagrams, state/mode diagrams, PVMT property/parameter definitions, budget simulations, early trade-study simulations, and other ARCADIA/PVMT artifacts; requirements tables/matrices and test procedures are not shown.

evidence_quotes: This paper presents the first version of the unified Modeling and Simulation (M&S) framework MOSAiC ... which connects MBSE with open source, multi-domain simulation environments, with the goal of improving traceability, reusability, and fidelity in the system lifecycle.
source_field_summaries.label: generality/reuse mechanism
rationales: MOSAiC is presented as a reusable framework/workflow rather than only the FIRE-EYE mission model. The paper explicitly claims applicability beyond a specific space application, uses layered abstraction from stakeholder needs to components, emphasizes interfaces/data exchanges between MBSE and simulations, and makes models/code publicly available. Do not code low-dynamics / non-detailed-behavior model because dynamic, time-dependent simulations are central; do not code specific-mission model with reusable method only because the framework itself is claimed adaptable beyond the case.

evidence_quotes: especially effective in the field of small-satellite missions, where resource constraints and short schedules require a quick and cheap way to perform "design and verification" iterations
source_field_summaries.label: tailoring rationale
rationales: Tailoring is justified by small-satellite scale, academic/resource-constrained contexts, short schedules, low-cost design/verification iterations, and open-source tool availability/preference.

evidence_quotes: As presented in the following sections, it is composed of two modules: the (i) System and Operation Modeling module and (ii) Analysis and Simulation module.
source_field_summaries.label: adoption guidance
rationales: The paper provides framework modules, ARCADIA levels, data flows, and an applied case, but not a full step-by-step adopter playbook with roles, entry/exit criteria, and governance.

evidence_quotes: The system modeling process followed the ARCADIA methodology, and it was implemented using the Capella tool.
source_field_summaries.label: MBSE language/method/tool
rationales: The central MBSE method/tool is Capella/ARCADIA, with PVMT add-on, custom Python parser, custom simulation framework, open-source assets, and additional domain simulations; SysML is background only.

evidence_quotes: interfacing with simulation tools through standardized data exchanges and co-simulation strategies
source_field_summaries.label: interoperability mechanisms
rationales: Interoperability is implemented through Capella-to-simulation data extraction/translation by a Python parser, simulation interfacing/co-simulation strategies, and model data import/export into domain analyses; specific standards/API details are limited.

evidence_quotes: Figures 12 and 13 illustrate this evolution using the Electrical Power Subsystem (EPS) as an example.
source_field_summaries.label: EPS relevance
rationales: The article is system-level, but it explicitly develops an EPS physical architecture example and power/battery simulations; EPS is important but not the sole paper focus.

evidence_quotes: During this process, critical design decisions were made, such as the selection of solar panels for power generation and the definition of battery subsystems for energy storage.
source_field_summaries.label: EPS elements modeled
rationales: The EPS example includes generation, storage, regulation/control/distribution, loads, modes, margins, budgets, fault handling, and power/communication interfaces; additional elements include sun sensors, SADA, MPPT, BMS, and PCDU/MCU details.

evidence_quotes: In the bottom right, the Simulation Environment block contains Analyses and Simulations, which include Design Space Exploration, Performance and Functional Verification, Operational Consistency Check, and Requirements Verification.
source_field_summaries.label: verification/validation artifacts
rationales: Verification is performed through scenario-based dynamic simulations and executable checks against requirements/preconditions/acceptable bounds; no verification matrix, test cases, procedures, or HIL artifacts are reported.

evidence_quotes: These simulations allow the early identification of performance shortfall, functional misalignment or unforeseen degradations, thereby enabling corrective actions well before hardware implementation.
source_field_summaries.label: pre-physical verification mechanism
rationales: Before hardware implementation, the model supports requirements-linked dynamic simulation, parametric budget checks, trade-space exploration, and virtual integration of subsystem interactions.

evidence_quotes: Unlike earlier qualitative/exploratory phases, this stage features a direct linkage between formal requirement specifications and simulation results.
source_field_summaries.label: IV&V integration level
rationales: The highest supported IVV integration level is simulation-in-the-loop: Capella/PVMT model data are extracted into dynamic simulations that check requirements, preconditions, power balance, battery sufficiency, and communication feasibility before hardware. Do not upgrade to software/hardware-in-the-loop because HIL/digital twin integration is only future work.

evidence_quotes: Overall, this early feedback loop enabled more informed and data-driven design decisions, provided justification for architectural refinements, and strengthened the confidence in the system's capacity to meet mission-level constraints
source_field_summaries.label: ROI/value evidence
rationales: The paper provides qualitative/simulation-backed decision-support evidence, but not cost of adoption, training effort, saved effort, schedule effects, avoided rework, or quantified reuse value.

label: Integrating Model-Based Systems Engineering into CubeSat Development: A Case Study of the BOREALIS Mission

evidence_quotes: The Biofilm Onboard Radiation Exposure Assessment Lab In Space (BOREALIS) mission is a 6U CubeSat initiative funded by the Italian Space Agency under the ALCOR program
source_field_summaries.label: development context
rationales: The mission is led by university groups with ASI/ENEA and Kayser Italy participation, across multiple organizations, and explicitly constrained as a low-cost, short-schedule 6U CubeSat using COTS.

evidence_quotes: This study explores the systematic application of Model-Based Systems Engineering to satellite design, from conceptualisation to trade-offs
source_field_summaries.label: lifecycle stage addressed
rationales: The MBSE work is applied to early concept formulation, trade-offs, Phase A/B design support, and CONOPS/mission operations planning, not to CDR, implementation, or flight operations results.

evidence_quotes: In the context of the BOREALIS mission, MBSE has been integral to aligning complex biological and engineering requirements within the constraints of a CubeSat platform. In the first stage of the mission, a satellite model to evaluate the performance of its different configurations has been developed
source_field_summaries.label: model maturity
rationales: The MAU/cost tradespace model is built and executed for the BOREALIS case with Monte Carlo and sensitivity analyses, but the later Valispace IDM is future work and the satellite is not operational.

evidence_quotes: In the context of the BOREALIS mission, MBSE has been integral to aligning complex biological and engineering requirements within the constraints of a CubeSat platform. In the first stage of the mission, a satellite model to evaluate the performance of its different configurations has been developed
source_field_summaries.label: approach classification
rationales: The approach is a system model plus selected analysis/simulation/trade-study support, with a planned data-management IDM; it is not yet an integrated digital engineering environment through downstream hardware/software verification.

evidence_quotes: Emphasis will be given to the model built for the tradeoff analysis, explaining how it was built and used and providing the reader with all the elements to possibly reuse it for another mission design of the same satellite class.
source_field_summaries.label: RQ1 relevance
rationales: The core contribution is a reusable system-level MBSE/tradespace workflow for a 6U CubeSat mission and includes power-architecture decisions.

evidence_quotes: Concept 10 maintains its relative position as a robust and cost-effective solution, with minimal variability in both utility and cost with respect to the other concepts.
source_field_summaries.label: RQ2 relevance
rationales: The paper claims robustness, decision support, traceability, and reuse at nanosatellite system level; these are not derived from a detailed EPS model.

evidence_quotes: Development and Verification Plans: Strategic documents that outline the procedures for system validation against the mission requirements and operational readiness checks.
source_field_summaries.label: RQ3 relevance
rationales: The paper includes pre-physical trade-study and validation-planning elements, but does not present an EPS IVV model or integrated EPS verification procedure.

evidence_quotes: Regarding the design process, starting from the scientific objectives of the mission, the mission requirements and constraints have been identified to understand the possible choice on each satellite subsystem for the CubeSat configuration.
source_field_summaries.label: modeling scope
rationales: The model links mission/science requirements to subsystem ADs, budget/performance variables, mission profile/CONOPS, simulations, and tradespace optimization; 'other' captures MAU/cost tradespace decision analysis.

evidence_quotes: In Figure 3, a summary of the SE process is reported, including the specific deliverables that we chose to manage the mission in accordance with ASI.
source_field_summaries.label: model artifacts used
rationales: Reported artifacts include requirements documents/tables, MAU/cost parametric functions, AD/concept trade-study models, power/energy performance variables, and GMAT/FLUKA/Monte Carlo simulations.

evidence_quotes: Emphasis will be given to the model built for the tradeoff analysis, explaining how it was built and used and providing the reader with all the elements to possibly reuse it for another mission design of the same satellite class.
source_field_summaries.label: generality/reuse mechanism
rationales: The reusable contribution is a high-level architectural-decision and MAU/cost trade-study workflow with adaptation guidance for similar CubeSat missions. The actual model is BOREALIS-specific and requires retuning of ADs, weights, utility/cost functions, and performance parameters; it is not a mission-agnostic architecture, template, open package, interface-focused model, or detailed reusable behavior model.

label: Preliminary Design of Satellite Systems through the Integration of Model-Based System Engineering and Agile Methodologies: Application to the 3ColStar Mission

evidence_quotes: developed collaboratively by the Colombian Aerospace Force (COLAF), Colombian universities, and other international institutions
source_field_summaries.label: development context
rationales: The project involves Colombian universities, the Colombian Aerospace Force, companies/start-ups, and many institutions; it uses Agile/Scrum and is motivated by small-satellite resource constraints and distributed collaboration.

evidence_quotes: Agile practices during two critical phases of the 3ColStar project: the proposal structuring and preliminary design stages.
source_field_summaries.label: lifecycle stage addressed
rationales: The paper covers proposal/concept and preliminary design of a 1U CubeSat, maps NASA design phases, and models ConOps/operations modes; no implementation, I&T, or flight results are reported.

evidence_quotes: Each subsystem of the satellite was designed and integrated into the Capella model
source_field_summaries.label: model maturity
rationales: The Arcadia/Capella model is applied to the 3ColStar mission preliminary design; the satellite has not been manufactured or flown.

evidence_quotes: Requirements were established initially from mission concept, translated into Capella, and linked to various model elements
source_field_summaries.label: approach classification
rationales: The central Capella/Arcadia system model is extended across requirements, logical/physical architecture, subsystem analyses, test/validation links, governance, and operations, but automated cross-tool digital-thread integration is not demonstrated.

evidence_quotes: This paper presents a case study ... focusing on the 3ColStar satellite mission.
source_field_summaries.label: RQ1 relevance
rationales: The paper presents a project-applied system-level MBSE architecture for a 1U nanosatellite and includes EPS architecture/power budget, but it is a mission case rather than a general minimal-knowledge modeling method.

evidence_quotes: By adopting this methodology, we ensured that the 3ColStar mission's technical and operational feasibility was thoroughly assessed and optimized from the early stages of development, leading to a more reliable satellite design.
source_field_summaries.label: RQ2 relevance
rationales: The paper claims reliability, traceability, communication, efficiency, consistency, and integration outcomes from MBSE/agile system modeling, but does not isolate EPS-specific reliability/reproducibility/integrability outcomes.

evidence_quotes: From the component to system level, each part was linked to test cases and validation criteria
source_field_summaries.label: RQ3 relevance
rationales: Verification and validation links, test cases, validation criteria, simulations, and requirements traceability are described before physical implementation, but no detailed EPS-specific verification procedure model is provided.

evidence_quotes: models that contain requirements, architecture, and interfaces between the different parts of the system
source_field_summaries.label: modeling scope
rationales: The Capella/Arcadia model covers mission needs, system/subsystem architecture, EPS power budgets, operational behavior, interfaces, V&V/test cases, simulation-supported analyses, and project-management/governance aspects.

evidence_quotes: Table A1. 3ColStar requirements.
source_field_summaries.label: model artifacts used
rationales: The paper reports requirements tables/viewpoints, logical/physical architecture block diagrams, state-machine-style operational modes, analyses/parametric tables, interface/physical link diagrams, power budgets, linked test cases, orbital/thermal simulations, and Capella traceability/coverage matrices.

evidence_quotes: This paper presents a case study on integrating Agile Systems Engineering methodologies in the preliminary design phase of satellite systems, focusing on the 3ColStar satellite mission.
source_field_summaries.label: generality/reuse mechanism
rationales: The paper is a 3ColStar-specific case study. Its reusable contribution is the Arcadia/Capella plus Agile workflow and guidance, not a reusable mission-agnostic model, template, library, open package, or reference architecture. High-level/logical abstraction and interface modeling are present, but the paper does not demonstrate those model features as reusable beyond this mission.
values: specific-mission model with reusable method only

evidence_quotes: small satellite projects are often limited in terms of funding, personnel resources, and timescale
source_field_summaries.label: tailoring rationale
rationales: Tailoring is justified by small-satellite constraints, limited resources, accelerated design timing, risk mitigation, dynamic requirements, and the need to coordinate universities/organizations with different capabilities.

evidence_quotes: Arcadia is built around the following statements
source_field_summaries.label: adoption guidance
rationales: The paper gives Arcadia stages, Capella integration steps, traceability mechanisms, Agile/Scrum tailoring, and governance roles, but not a complete adopter playbook with prerequisites and completion criteria for every step.

evidence_quotes: The MBSE approach utilized SysML and Arcadia/Capella frameworks
source_field_summaries.label: MBSE language/method/tool
rationales: The paper reports SysML and Arcadia/Capella for MBSE, Capella 6.1 as open-source, and STK/GMAT/MATLAB/Simulink/DRAMA plus other domain tools for validation and analysis.

evidence_quotes: Requirements were imported and hierarchically structured within Capella's Requirement Viewpoint
source_field_summaries.label: interoperability mechanisms
rationales: Requirements are imported/structured in Capella, and model updates are manually governed by system engineers based on weekly meetings; no API, co-simulation, XMI/ReqIF, or automated transformation is described.

evidence_quotes: Electric Power Systems-Power Budget
source_field_summaries.label: EPS relevance
rationales: EPS is not the sole focus, but the paper includes EPS physical architecture, power generation/storage/distribution functions, solar panels, batteries, modes, and detailed power budgets.

evidence_quotes: Physical Components: solar panels, batteries, and power management units (PMUs).
source_field_summaries.label: EPS elements modeled
rationales: The EPS representation includes solar arrays, battery pack, power controller/distribution, subsystem loads by operating mode, power budgets, and EPS links to other subsystems.

evidence_quotes: each part was linked to test cases and validation criteria
source_field_summaries.label: verification/validation artifacts
rationales: The paper reports test cases and validation criteria linked to design elements and uses orbital, thermal, and link-budget simulations; it does not provide full executable test procedures.

evidence_quotes: Although actual manufacturing of the subsystems has not yet started
source_field_summaries.label: pre-physical verification mechanism
rationales: Before physical manufacturing, requirements and physical/logical elements are linked in the model; orbital, link-budget, thermal, and power-budget analyses act as simulation/parametric checks; the unified Capella model supports virtual subsystem integration.

evidence_quotes: Bidirectional traceability was established ... by creating traceability links between the requirements and their associated system functions, logical components, and verification test cases.
source_field_summaries.label: IV&V integration level
rationales: The paper reports Capella trace links from requirements to functions, components, verification test cases, and validation criteria. It also reports external analyses/simulations, but does not show tool connections, executable model-based checks, simulation-in-the-loop integration, SIL/HIL, or physical test evidence. Therefore the current simulation-in-the-loop coding is overstated.

evidence_quotes: comprehensive design activities were undertaken to lay a solid foundation for future development and integration
source_field_summaries.label: integration/test readiness
rationales: The physical architecture and linked validation criteria are intended to support future subsystem manufacturing/integration, and operational modes/ConOps are modeled; no flat-sat, environmental-test, or flight validation is reported.

evidence_quotes: Two designated System Engineers were assigned critical roles in model governance.
source_field_summaries.label: model governance strategy
rationales: The paper reports lead/secondary system engineers, subsystem representatives, permissions, project-manager authorization of critical changes, weekly meetings, and integrity/traceability/consistency as governance aims.

evidence_quotes: enabled the completion of this process within a remarkable timeframe of just 4 months
source_field_summaries.label: ROI/value evidence
rationales: The paper claims a 4-month preliminary design schedule and avoided design rework, but provides no cost-benefit calculation or adoption-cost data.

evidence_quotes: As part of the FP7 QB50 consortium, the Delft University of Technology participates to the QB50 mission by supplying two nano-satellites, called De and Phi, which form the space segment of the DelFFi mission.
source_field_summaries.label: development context
rationales: The case is a TU Delft mission and includes an educational/student objective; other contexts are not directly evidenced.

evidence_quotes: In this step, detailed technical requirements are developed, and integrated system models including requirement model and ADCS models are built ... early development phase, i.e. Phase-A or B ... For each iteration, verification using SysM or executable SysML driven simulations shall be performed.
source_field_summaries.label: lifecycle stage addressed
rationales: The method explicitly covers early Phase A/B requirement/model iterations, later onboard/flight software development, HIL/FM testing, and an operational target for generated software; operations are a downstream target, not operational evidence.

evidence_quotes: The definition of guidelines associated to a welldefined template is observed to be of vital importa in order to apply the MBSE approach, and to actual make the model reusable.
source_field_summaries.label: model maturity
rationales: The paper proposes a methodology/template, applies it to DelFFi, and demonstrates executable SysML/Simulink verification; downstream software integration is partly conceptual/proposed.

evidence_quotes: A collaborative MBSE workspace/environment is provided. This workspace integrates discipline-specific models capable of performing all aspects of the system definition. With proper construction of Simulink models and wrap-up of engineering model and flight model of onboard software, this workspace even allows a seamless integration of requirement development, model verification, code automatic generation and verification with high efficiency and quality.
source_field_summaries.label: approach classification
rationales: The described environment links SysML requirements, executable simulation, MATLAB/Simulink, generated C code, code verification, HIL/FM integration, and testing.

evidence_quotes: This paper aims at filling the aforementioned ... misalignment by utilizing Model-Based Systems ... Engineering (MBSE) in support of nano-satellite development. Using the DelFFi mission of the Delft ... University of Technology (TUD) as a case study ... focuses on two particular aspects of applying ... MBSE: requirements development and design ... validation, and their link with onboard software development.
source_field_summaries.label: RQ1 relevance
rationales: The paper's main contribution is a SysML/MBSE methodology and template for nanosatellite requirements, system/subsystem modeling, and design verification.

evidence_quotes: Using this three-step approach, The ADCS models developed earlier can be re-used, and the engineers can focus more on developing the models rather than programming. A second benefit is the increase in quality of the codes since the consistency of the simulation models and the onboard software is structurally assured.
source_field_summaries.label: RQ2 relevance
rationales: The paper claims reuse, consistency, quality, and integration benefits from MBSE, but mostly for nanosatellite/ADCS rather than EPS-specific outcomes.

evidence_quotes: To automatically verify the ADCS design satisfy requirements, simulations are performed from SysML, aiming at investigating the satellite behavior in the five ADCS modes, i.e. detumble, coarse sun pointing, fine sun pointing, thruster pointing and ground station tracking. Here only the verification the detumble mode is presented.
source_field_summaries.label: RQ3 relevance
rationales: The paper integrates pre-physical verification through executable SysML and Simulink for ADCS/system requirements; it does not present an EPS verification procedure model.

evidence_quotes: This paper presented a gap-filling methodology utilizing Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) in support of nano-satellite development. Using a satellite mission as case study, this paper focuses two particular aspects of applying MBSE: requirements development and design validation, and their linkinboard software development.
source_field_summaries.label: modeling scope
rationales: Scope covers mission/system/subsystem requirements, ADCS behavior and simulation verification, subsystem power budgets/EPS mention, and downstream software/HIL/FM/operation workflow; 'other' captures onboard software/code generation.

evidence_quotes: For the case study of DelFFi, the following requirement stereotypes are created: Customer Need Statement ... Mission Requirement ... System Requirement
source_field_summaries.label: model artifacts used
rationales: Reported artifacts include SysML requirement diagrams/tables, block/constraint/parametric modeling, power-budget-related requirements, executable Simulink simulations, plus object/model instances, stereotypes, and generated C code captured as 'other'.

evidence_quotes: The definition of guidelines associated to a welldefined template is observed to be of vital importa in order to apply the MBSE approach, and to actual make the model reusable.
source_field_summaries.label: generality/reuse mechanism
rationales: The paper supports reusable templates/guidelines, step workflows, and MATLAB/Simulink model libraries, but the demonstrated SysML/executable case remains DelFFi/ADCS-specific. Do not retain interface-focused model: interfaces/tool links are present, but the reuse mechanism is not an interface-focused architecture. Do not add high-level abstraction, mission-agnostic architecture, or low-dynamics / non-detailed-behavior model; detailed ADCS dynamics and mission-specific parameters are central.

evidence_quotes: It includes numerous requirement blocks such as ... 'Solar Power,' 'Volume Budget,' 'Power Budget,' ADCS-Processing ...
source_field_summaries.label: EPS elements modeled
rationales: Power-budget requirements appear in the system/ADCS requirement models; detailed EPS element modeling is otherwise not shown.

evidence_quotes: To automatically verify the ADCS design satisfy requirements, simulations are performed from SysML, aiming at investigating the satellite behavior in the five ADCS modes, i.e. detumble, coarse sun pointing, fine sun pointing, thruster pointing and ground station tracking. Here only the verification the detumble mode is presented.
source_field_summaries.label: verification/validation artifacts
rationales: The demonstrated artifacts include ADCS mode simulation scenarios, a detumble acceptance criterion, executable requirement-status checking, and planned HIL/code-verification links; these are not EPS-specific.

evidence_quotes: ADCSF.34 is connected to a constraint block by means of 'refine' relationship. This is the way SysML adopts indicate that a requirement can be analyzed executi parametric models.
source_field_summaries.label: pre-physical verification mechanism
rationales: Before hardware, SysML requirements are refined to parametric constraints and checked by SysML-driven MATLAB/Simulink simulation; this is demonstrated for ADCS rather than EPS.

evidence_quotes: ADCSF.34 is connected to a constraint block by means of 'refine' relationship. This is the way SysML adopts indicate that a requirement can be analyzed executi parametric models.
source_field_summaries.label: IV&V integration level
rationales: The highest demonstrated integration level is SysML-driven MATLAB/Simulink simulation-in-the-loop for ADCS/system verification: a requirement is refined to a constraint, tool-connected simulation runs, and results update SysML requirement status. The HIL/flight-model path is described as a downstream/foreseen workflow and should not be the coded highest level. No EPS-specific IVV is demonstrated.

evidence_quotes: In this step, the ADCS models that have been developed as Simulink blocks for early stage phases and verified using executable SysML are translated automatically to hardware-independent C codes, which are then integrated with low layers of ADCS onboard software to perform Hardware-in-loop simulations.
source_field_summaries.label: integration/test readiness
rationales: The workflow connects generated ADCS code to lower software layers, HIL simulations, and a hardware Flight Model; actual integration/test evidence is not reported.

source_field_summaries.label: model governance strategy
rationales: The paper does not report model ownership, configuration/change control, review process, model quality criteria, or naming/versioning conventions.

evidence_quotes: Using the Model Driven development procedure defined above and the supporting simulation platform, the AOCS/GNC designer can reduce the time to design the system while an even more reliab outcome is guaranteed.
source_field_summaries.label: ROI/value evidence
rationales: The paper claims efficiency and reduced design time but provides no adoption cost, saved effort, schedule, rework, or ROI evidence.

evidence_quotes: We have used SysML to develop a scalable model repository for RS satellites.
source_field_summaries.label: RQ1 relevance
rationales: The paper centrally develops a SysML/OOSEM system model repository for a nanosatellite-class remote-sensing student satellite and emphasizes reusable/generic modeling patterns.

evidence_quotes: The repository illuminates a path to an integrated model-based engineering environment, including interoperability with existing SE models ready in existing analysis tools such as Microsoft Excel, MATLAB, and STK.
source_field_summaries.label: RQ2 relevance
rationales: The paper claims traceability, consistency, interoperability, reuse, risk and productivity outcomes, but provides limited EPS-specific reliability/reproducibility/integrability evidence.

evidence_quotes: constraint blocks have been created to calculate the mass and power margins in the budgets ... depicted in the SysML requirement diagram with the verify relationship
source_field_summaries.label: RQ3 relevance
rationales: The paper integrates requirements verification and parametric checks for mass/power budgets before physical development, but does not present detailed EPS verification procedures or tests.

evidence_quotes: Figure 1 ... MBSE Artifacts used ... Mission use cases / scenarios ... Requirement Diagrams ... Internal Block Diagrams ... Parametric Diagrams ... State Machines ... Unit, Subsystem and System Test cases and V&V.
source_field_summaries.label: modeling scope
rationales: The SysML repository covers mission scenarios/use cases, system and subsystem architecture/behavior, interface descriptions, mass/power/reliability budgets, requirements verification, operational modes, code/simulation concepts, and AIT artifacts. EPS scope is limited to block-level power budget.

evidence_quotes: The NSS-1 model is developed using diverse SysML diagrams.
source_field_summaries.label: model artifacts used
rationales: Reported artifacts include SysML requirements, BDD/IBD, state/activity/sequence, parametric budget diagrams, trade/design-space exploration, interface diagrams, power budgets, test cases, verification matrices, generated tables/reports; other captures package/use-case diagrams and reliability/orbital/FOV analyses.

evidence_quotes: We have used SysML to develop a scalable model repository for RS satellites. A parametric model-based approach has been used that allows generic models of various mission scenarios to be characterized for the study being performed.
source_field_summaries.label: generality/reuse mechanism
rationales: The paper supports reuse through FireSat model-element reuse, common nanosatellite design patterns, OOSEM/PNSSP method guidance, and high-level/generic mission-scenario abstraction. It should not be coded as mission-agnostic architecture, interface-focused model, or low-dynamics / non-detailed-behavior model. The implemented case is NSS-1, but the paper claims model/pattern reuse beyond NSS-1, so 'specific-mission model with reusable method only' is too restrictive.

evidence_quotes: The methodology fits with the evolutionary nature of our projects and their life cycles within the organization.
source_field_summaries.label: tailoring rationale
rationales: Tailoring is motivated by small/nanosatellite PNSSP context, conventional engineers' learning needs, early parameter freeze, existing Office/STK/MATLAB tools, and organizational lifecycle fit.

evidence_quotes: OOSEM-based methodology as adopted is depicted in Figure 1, showing satellite design and development project activities, along with corresponding modeling artifacts used.
source_field_summaries.label: adoption guidance
rationales: The paper gives phase-artifact mapping and a two-step PNSSP adoption approach but not a complete adopter playbook with roles, completion criteria, and templates.

evidence_quotes: We used MagicDraw 18.1 from No Magic Inc. [16] as the modeling tool and SysML 1.4 as the modeling language.
source_field_summaries.label: MBSE language/method/tool
rationales: Central toolchain elements are SysML 1.4, MagicDraw, MATLAB/Simulink, STK, prior custom SIDE/Excel environment; other captures OOSEM, ParaMagic, InterCAX, Excel, and MATLAB SMT solver.

evidence_quotes: With the help of MagicDraw plug-ins, we are able to communicate between existing engineering analysis tools with the NSS1 model repository
source_field_summaries.label: interoperability mechanisms
rationales: Explicit mechanisms include MagicDraw plug-ins, Excel import/export and spreadsheets, MATLAB functions/scripts with output files read back into SysML, intermediary MATLAB script for Simulink, and generated code structure.

evidence_quotes: Additional modeling challenges are associated with scaling the modeling effort to larger projects and in the context of a diverse development environment.
source_field_summaries.label: toolchain limitations
rationales: Authors identify integration/scaling challenges and leave direct STK-SysML interface to future work.

evidence_quotes: The ACS ... CDHS ... payload, TCS ... and RFCS ... subsystems draw electrical power from the EPS (Electrical power subsystem), which can supply a maximum of 80 W.
source_field_summaries.label: EPS relevance
rationales: EPS appears as a subsystem and power supplier in system power budget verification, not as a detailed EPS design model.

evidence_quotes: subsystems draw electrical power from the EPS (Electrical power subsystem), which can supply a maximum of 80 W
source_field_summaries.label: EPS elements modeled
rationales: EPS representation is limited to power supplied by EPS to subsystem loads, power budget constraints, and power/mass margins; no solar array, battery, degradation, or detailed EPS architecture is reported.

evidence_quotes: The requirement diagram defines requirements, traceability, and the test cases that verify each requirement.
source_field_summaries.label: verification/validation artifacts
rationales: The model uses test cases and verification matrices generally, and executable constraint checks against mass/power requirements with threshold acceptance criteria.

evidence_quotes: constraint blocks have been created to calculate the mass and power margins in the budgets ... depicted in the SysML requirement diagram with the verify relationship
source_field_summaries.label: pre-physical verification mechanism
rationales: Before physical development, requirements are linked to constraint blocks and checked by ParaMagic/MATLAB SMT mass/power budget calculations.

evidence_quotes: The requirement diagram defines requirements, traceability, and the test cases that verify each requirement.
source_field_summaries.label: IV&V integration level
rationales: The highest supported IVV integration level is executable/model-based checks: SysML requirements are linked by verify relationships to constraint blocks, and ParaMagic/MATLAB SMT solves the mass/power margins. This is not simulation-in-the-loop, SIL/HIL, or detailed EPS test integration.

evidence_quotes: This code can be used to develop prototype models for simulation of the system. For software-based models, the code structure can be directly used for implementation of operations and functions by software developers.
source_field_summaries.label: integration/test readiness
rationales: Readiness is reported mainly at system/software level through generated code structure and test-case traceability; hardware/flat-sat/environmental links are not shown.

label: Automating Object-Oriented Functional Modeling for Standardized Design in the New Space Domain

evidence_quotes: The approach is tailored to the modular and service-oriented context of the New Space sector
source_field_summaries.label: development context
rationales: The method is explicitly tailored to the New Space/Satellite-as-a-Service industrial context and the pilot is conducted with an industry small-satellite manufacturer. Agile development is discussed as an intended System-as-Code benefit, but an actual agile/concurrent project setting is not documented enough to code it as development context.

evidence_quotes: The model begins at the Operational Analysis (OA) level, defining the overall space program context and mission objectives.
source_field_summaries.label: lifecycle stage addressed
rationales: The model spans early operational analysis, system analysis, logical architecture, and physical architecture definition; it is an early architecture/model-generation method rather than an integration/test or operations report.

evidence_quotes: the paper presents the modeling theory and validation of an automated object-oriented modeling framework
source_field_summaries.label: model maturity
rationales: The contribution combines modeling theory and reusable baseline/library concepts with a pilot demonstration; no validated operational or flight model is reported.

evidence_quotes: The automated workflow developed in this work demonstrated the feasibility of integrating functional analysis, reuse of standard structures, and model-data interaction across abstraction layers.
source_field_summaries.label: approach classification
rationales: The approach connects model layers, functional libraries, automation scripts/APIs, external data sources, and digital-thread concepts across multiple abstraction levels, but does not demonstrate a full integrated environment including downstream hardware/software integration or verification evidence.

evidence_quotes: this paper proposes an object-oriented functional approach for managing satellite platform digitalization in a modular and reusable manner through functional grouping
source_field_summaries.label: RQ1 relevance
rationales: The paper centrally addresses reusable/general satellite platform modeling for New Space missions through object-oriented functional grouping, standard baselines, and automated model generation; it is not EPS-specific but is directly relevant to nanosatellite/small-satellite system modeling generality.

evidence_quotes: An automated object-oriented systems engineering approach... has proven effective in enhancing model modularity, traceability, and replicability in the context of the New Space scenario.
source_field_summaries.label: RQ2 relevance
rationales: The paper claims MBSE-related reproducibility, reuse, consistency, traceability, and interoperability outcomes, but these are system/platform-level and not EPS-specific reliability/reproducibility/integrability outcomes.

evidence_quotes: Further work may explore the integration of automated functional verification mechanisms to complement the structural and semantic validation demonstrated in this study
source_field_summaries.label: RQ3 relevance
rationales: The paper does not present EPS verification procedure modeling prior to physical development; it explicitly leaves automated functional verification mechanisms to future work.

evidence_quotes: The model begins at the Operational Analysis (OA) level, defining the overall space program context and mission objectives.
source_field_summaries.label: modeling scope
rationales: The modeled scope includes OA mission/stakeholder context, satellite-platform system and subsystem capability groups, requirements/stakeholder linkage, functional/logical/physical architecture, functions/behavior and interfaces, mission phases/operations, possible system budgeting, and the additional System-as-Code automation/digital-thread scope captured as other.

evidence_quotes: Functional Elements, Functional Interfaces, and Functional Connections... Component Elements, Component Interfaces, and Component Connections
source_field_summaries.label: model artifacts used
rationales: Reported artifacts include functional/component interfaces and exchanges, parametric groups/property values, and Capella-specific capability, functional, logical, component, functional-library, and API artifacts not named in the controlled list.

evidence_quotes: An automated framework was developed to support fast, consistent deployment of satellite digital models across missions, leveraging standard solutions and use cases.
source_field_summaries.label: generality/reuse mechanism
rationales: The paper supports cross-mission reuse through reusable baselines/templates, reference/model patterns, functional libraries, and an automated Capella/Python4Capella workflow. The reusable architecture is high-level and mission-agnostic enough to be imported and extended for mission-specific elements, and interfaces/exchanges are a central organizing mechanism. Do not retain low-dynamics / non-detailed-behavior model: the paper uses functional abstraction, but does not explicitly make low-dynamics or non-detailed behavior a reuse mechanism.

evidence_quotes: The New Space Economy is characterized by the use of standardized and miniaturized components... enable cost-efficient space system solutions
source_field_summaries.label: tailoring rationale
rationales: Tailoring is justified by New Space small-satellite standardization, fast/cost-effective deployment needs, the Satellite-as-a-Service/platform-provider organization, and Capella/Python4Capella automation capability.

evidence_quotes: The implementation strategy is structured around three core components
source_field_summaries.label: adoption guidance
rationales: The paper provides a structured method and automation architecture, but not a full adopter playbook with prerequisites, roles, completion criteria, or lifecycle gate instructions.

evidence_quotes: ARCADIA... natively deployed in the open-source tool Capella
source_field_summaries.label: MBSE language/method/tool
rationales: The core toolchain is Capella/ARCADIA plus Python/Python4Capella and custom APIs/classes. Open-source Capella/Python4Capella ecosystem tools are central. Other captures FAS, System as Code, OOP, PVMT, Filtering Add-On, and structured data formats.

evidence_quotes: Python scripts are used to to read and write from/to the Capella model
source_field_summaries.label: interoperability mechanisms
rationales: Interoperability is implemented through Python4Capella/custom APIs, Python scripts, structured data imports/exports including Excel/JSON/YAML/spreadsheets, and bidirectional data flow with external sources.

evidence_quotes: This strategy let the user copy and paste manually elements from a project to another.
source_field_summaries.label: toolchain limitations
rationales: The authors report native manual copy/paste reuse, gaps in Capella APIs/add-on interfaces requiring custom APIs, Capella static/code-model limitations, and scalability/maintainability problems in manually built functional libraries.

evidence_quotes: Spacecrafts are typically composed of recurring functional subsystems, such as... power supply
source_field_summaries.label: EPS relevance
rationales: Power/EPS appears as one subsystem concern and illustrative physical-architecture example; the paper is about satellite platform functional modeling, not a dedicated EPS model.

evidence_quotes: the model can emphasize specific concerns such as electric power regulation and distribution mapping
source_field_summaries.label: EPS elements modeled
rationales: Power/EPS content is limited to illustrative or optional subsystem concerns: power-demanding components/loads, Provide Power capability, PCDU, and electrical/power distribution mapping and interfaces.

evidence_quotes: The validation process focused iteratively on four main areas: satellite platform modeling, functional library development, digital thread, and automation.
source_field_summaries.label: IV&V integration level
rationales: No EPS or system IVV artifacts are integrated into the model. The reported checks are manual inspection and Capella structural/semantic validation of generated model elements, while automated functional verification is explicitly future work.

evidence_quotes: A System as Code practice allows for an agile system development with automated workflow and configuration management of the digital thread
source_field_summaries.label: model governance strategy
rationales: The paper discusses configuration management/150% variability and evaluates model-generation quality using correctness, omissions, semantic correctness, structural consistency, and Capella validation; it does not report ownership or versioning governance.
